annotations.text:
Sourced from Mobbin's command-palette pattern set, Raycast's 2026 rebuild, Fig's terminal overlay, and the terminal-native pickers.

Headline: nobody ships a chromeless command palette. Mobbin studied 120+ and not one is borderless.

The placement board on the right is the one that changes the plan.

Worst first.

01 and 02 can each sink the direction on their own. 02 is the one that surprised me — if motion is the chrome, Reduce Motion leaves nothing at all.

Everything from 03 down is work, not risk.

Cheapest next move is 03: ten seconds of capture with a build running.

Five states, all over live terminal output.

The thing to judge here is not whether it looks clean — it will. It is whether you can tell, at a glance, that you are in a mode at all.

Two forks are called out inline: centred vs. left-aligned at the caret (02), and sub-range tinting at the macOS 13 floor (03).

Your question was what hints someone gets.

Answer: three of the four already ship, and the ghost placeholder is the strongest hint in the product — it renders the exact path Return would commit.

The one real hole is rung 2, and PR #155 opened it, not this direction. Fix is one keystroke: ↓ reveals the list.

Three boards animate; let them loop a few times.

The governing rule is on the spec sheet: blur leads text going in, trails it coming out. That single ordering is what makes this read as a mode rather than a popup.

Nothing here exceeds 180ms.
